Cover Art, Graphics and Game Design by Trevor Storey. 

Music by Andrew Fisher. 

Tape loader source by Martin Piper. 

Tape mastering by Richard Bayliss. 

Additional packaging design by Kenz.

174220.overview:
Psytronik Software proudly presents SUPER CARLING THE SPIDER - a specially enhanced C64 conversion of the popular VIC-20 release! This is a multi-screen platform game featuring a little spider called Carling. Your mission is to collect all the shiny diamonds on each screen while avoiding deadly spikes and marauding BALLS OF STEEL! Once you have collected all the diamonds you must head to the exit in order to reach the next level. 

** SUPER CARLING THE SPIDER STORY ** 

Following his adventures on the VIC-20, Carling The Spider is BACK, this time on the C64! Super Carling The Spider is packed with new levels to explore, improved graphics and presentation, new soundtracks, enhanced gameplay features and much more!

Take control of Carling The Spider as he once again faces the dreaded BALLS OF STEEL!  Help him on his quest to reclaim the lost Rockford diamonds, and to clear the name of the Diamond Girls, who were originally framed for their mysterious disappearance!

174311.overview:
A vertically scrolling shooter where you are the lone pilot of a spaceship, your mission is to reach the heart of the enemy attack system at the end of a narrow tunnel. This corridor is extremely dangerous as it is protected from meteorites and space vehicles of various kinds. As you maneuver to avoid obstacles, fire lasers to destroy or at least keep enemy forces away, keep the energy level constant by traversing the energy stars, and rejoin your mothership to continue the daring mission. 

Published in Italy as Corridoio Nemico in the Super Game 2000 n.6 (luglio/agosto 1985) compilation.

174456.overview: A Pac-Man clone published in 64'er 1992/12. In this version there is no ghost home area and not cross-maze tunnels. Ghosts spawn from other ghosts or from the center of the map.

174927.overview:
Antonia Savona has done it again. Another stellar conversion of an Atari 2600 Activision classic to the C64. First there was his excellent conversion of Chopper Command, then there was Keystone Kapers, then Frostbite. Now comes his fourth conversion, a conversion of Dan Kitchen's classic game Crackpots.

Game's description:

A barrage of bugs are attacking your home, and you need to defend it with potted plants!

You control your character at the top of the screen where there are six potted plants. These can be dropped on the bugs to destroy them as they make their way up from the sewer at the bottom. Just beneath the potted plants are six windows; you need to make sure you destroy the bugs before they can reach these windows. If six of the bugs make it into the windows, a layer of your house will be eaten. This will drop you one step closer to the bottom of the screen, making it more difficult to destroy the incoming bugs! There are four different color bugs in the game, each of which have a different pattern of movement. As the levels progress, bugs will keep coming faster and faster!

The game ends when six layers of the building have been eaten.

174957.overview: An over head racing game for one player from Michael Meiszl originally released in the German Tiger-Crew-Disk #028 (07/1996) and later in Courbois Software #6421 / a.k.a. "Auto Race". Both games are loosely based on an earlier PET game of some renowned.

174959.overview: A single player, German language game, set on a racing track where the goal is to scoop up the pellets racing in one direction around the four-ringed track while avoiding cars racing around it in the opposite direction.

174960.overview: An educational game that teaches number recognition and teaches about places, like first through sixth, first place and last place in the race. Before and after and so forth. It simulates a race, then quizzes your child on who came in first, who came in last in the race. Who in before car number 3. Who came in after car number 1, etc.

174963.overview: A game where the challenge is to stay on the road while it curves all around you. A game by Mike Sleischner that was released in Frilly Disk #127 and with minor changes in other public domain compilations. Most likely created in the early 1980's, but the exact date of release is not currently known.

175193.overview: We should try to find a place to stay for the night. The horses need a rest. Those were the coachman's last words before he disappeared without a trace. Lost deep in the Black Forest, you soon find out that some things should remain buried forever. The Curse of Rabenstein is a new story by award-winning adventure author Stefan Vogt. Heavily inspired by the masterpieces from Level 9 and enhanced with stunning pixel graphics, this interactive horror will give you the shivers.

175500.overview:
Cloud King was developed in 2001 by Andrea Canobbio using Sensible Software's Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit. 

It was also entered into the 2003 SEUCK Compo with some minor graphical tweaking, which eventually lead the game to go on and win that year's compo, barely beating out the second place finisher (Renovator) by a 2 point margin.

Explore the cloud kingdom and face many deadly monsters in this cute action vertically scrolling shoot 'em up construction kit game.

175538.overview: A maze is quickly shown to you and then the fog of war sets in and you can only see the section of the map around you. How quickly can you get to the exit of the labyrinth and free yourself. Published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1984/06 (Issue #12), and Stonysoft #1912. Published in English and Dutch.

175554.overview: Published in micro Adventurer 1984/07 (Issue #09). A text adventure with 50,000 possible locations, so make sure you don't get lost. You have to make your way to the bottom of an old dungeon where you'll find a key to open all the gold-filled chests. beware of pits and creatures in the dungeon.

175555.overview: The moon base, CETI 21's security system was being upgraded. That was until a fatal computer crash on the mainframe has occurred. Now the force-field barrier has been shut down, and now the aliens have ransacked the computer. Defenses have turned against us. Luckily Ultrax 18 drones can be piloted by you. Your mission is to guide Ultrax 18 through all 3 zones in CETI 21. Fight your rogue defenses, and alien ships. Avoid shooting your own ships/drones. If you destroy any of these, you will have to pay the price of one of your precious lives. Can you reach the mainframe, and destroy it - and end the aliens ransacking CETI 21?

175556.overview: A game where you move around the game board based on correct answers trivia questions, a non-trivial pursuit by my estimation. The game board is a set of shoals your game boat token must move around and place over the fish to win.

175557.overview: A space-shooter game created using the Shoot 'Em Up Destruction\Construction Set with additional support for Hires-characters. With excellent music by Rock. Released to the scene by Finnish Gold.

175592.overview: An Arkanoid style Pong\Breakout game with money bricks that drop, you can use the money to buy special power ups that can help in clearing the level. Published in Italy in Special Program n.81 (novembre 1991), Computing videoteca Nuova serie - Mattoni Elettronici 2 and in Videoteca Computer n.31.

175761.overview: Less of a game and more of a performance art piece where you control the final work. Coccinelle Cherche Dessinateur means Ladybug Seeking Designer. The Ladybug is your cursor, you can change the colors of the bug and the trail that is created behind it, move around and create a pattern. Control the variables of what will appear on the screen.

175967.overview:
A nice German language C64 version of Mine Sweeper that accurately mimmicks the original Win3x version. Published in GO64! 1997/06.

The scene group Laxity translated it to English and released their version, later that same year.

176252.overview:
A Boulderdash clone game and second in a series by Reflectice Designs, it was published in Italy as Crokko in both Super C64 e C128 n.40 (dicembre 1989) and in Supplementi Edigamma/pubblirome - 100 games 90 (1990). 
 
The precious stones of Rockfall, which are indispensable for the production of energy, are starting to be scarce. It was therefore decided to send you to the mines again on the asteroids orbiting the Earth's Sun to recover some of these precious stones. The main difficulty consists in the presence of hostile alien beings, called Crokko, who can take a life from you if they touch you; furthermore, the stones are set in precarious positions and there is a constant risk that something will collapse when you try to extract them. You must recover a number of stones for each cave you visit (indicated at the bottom of the screen). After you reach the number you have to go back to the front door and enter it to go to the next more difficult cave. If you manage to make boulders fall on the aliens the turn into the precious stones you seek.

176267.overview: The original version left us wanting, specifically wanting the other 5 levels of play we enjoyed on the Coin-Op favorite. We also wanted a glitch free run. And while Commando 94 didn't give us all our heart's desires it did significantly better than the original 1985\1986 versions and infinitely better than the Space Invasion versions that German put out to be less violent by having us shoot silver cyborgs instead of enemy forces.

176276.overview: Commodore Force Pinball was a four player pinball game created with the Pinball Construction Set and was released as a homebrew game to the PCS Fan Club community in 1985.

176277.overview: A vertically scrolling Shoot'em Up created with the SEUCK and based on the 1988 sample called Transputer Man. However in this version the enemies are all sprites from Atari and Co games.

176278.overview:
A Boulder Dash style game where, like De Luxe Caves 3 and above, you can and must move diagonally in order to solve the game screen and move to the next one, unlike previous C64 games in this genre. But like other games in this style you have to dig through monster infested caves in search of diamonds. In each level you must collect a certain number of these diamonds, in order to open a portal to the next stage. Enemies can be squashed by falling boulders, which are released when the ground below them is removed or they are pushed onto empty ground, but be careful because these can also squash you. In later levels, difficulty is increased by many puzzle elements and shorter time limits. 
 
Most sites don't have a date for this release, but since it came out in conjunction with the Marek bugfixes and Version 2 Packer and it was the first of that type allowing diagonal movement it should be 1988. It is very likely that Crazy Dream 1 through 5 all came out at the same time.

176280.overview:
Crystal Caverns is a text-based adventure game for multiple systems.

The player arrived in front of an old Victorian mansion deep within the woods. Their goal is to search the forest and outlying buildings that surround the great house, and return all the treasures they find to the cupola of the house. Gameplay is via VERB NOUN text commands, and the player must map the world by hand. As the player explores the grounds, they find a hole which they can dig into the caverns that stretch far below the mansion. In these great caverns, a number of treasures, including: gold toothpicks, a sapphire, a painting, a ring, and more can be discovered. All of these must be returned to the mansion for the player to complete the game. The player must use care while exploring, as the wrong move can result in the death of the player.

At the end of each game, the player is awarded points for the number of areas they explored, turns used, and treasures recovered.

176393.overview: On the 10 year anniversary of the release of the original arcade game the Champion Software SEUCK crew tried to make this remake just a bit better with less errors and more gameplay that simulated the original as best as could be done at the time on the C64.

176559.overview:
A text adventure game published as a type-in game in the book "Castles & Kingdoms". 

The sword Deathtouch was alive. It sensed the darkness and the coolness of the stone. It was self-aware and in that awareness lay a sense of duty. The sword Deathtouch was Chaos incarnate. True to its name, no living creature could survive after being dealt a wound from its edge or point. The sword Deathtouch was a prisoner in the Realm of the Dead, a fitting place for it. For what death could it deal to those beyond life? What torture could it inflict on those tortured beyond the grave? The sword Deathtouch had not tasted warm blood for a long time. Butwarm bloods were crossing the river. Soon the blade of Chaos would be among the living, and many would die. The Priests of the Snake were nervous, as they had cause to be in this creepy sub-dungeon of Castle Northstar. And the High Priest, though outwardly confident, quivered in his robes at the misty waters of the river Styx. This was a spellbound place, the only place in the kingdom where the living joined the dead. The ferryman was Death' s minion; and the Ruler of the Dead was a shade of evil-a shadow of Alabastria, the Black Kingdom beyond the doors of Star gate. He held the keys to unlocking the Demons of Chaos and, by the tongue of the Snake, those keys would ride the ferry in the pocket of a red cloak. The girl was Human. She was too young to have reason for fright. The tall Priest spoke kindly to her and allowed no one near her but the two young guards. They never spoke at all. The Pries t had given her a bracelet and promised her another if she was good. She missed her father but she did not cry. She'd seen many wonders on her journey and had not had time to think of her family. She couldn't see much here because of the fog. She could hear strange sounds though, moaning in pain, softly whispering in agony through the mist. She was now a little frightened and moved closer to the High Priest, her protector. She wanted to cry but she could not. She could feel the tears within her but she could not cry. So the mist and the unseen voices cried for her, as though they knew her fate. The ferry cut through the dark water and through the hovering mist, bumped into the shore and grounded. The Priests and the girl disembarked and moved away from the shore. The ferry backed away and turned into the mists, the single oar of the ferryman rippling the water very slightly. The ferry moved across the river as if its pilot could see through the mists. Maybe he could. It stopped on the opposite shore and awaited its next passenger. The sword Deathtouch could sense the approaching Priests, warm bloods all. A deal had been struck that would return it to the upper world. Soon it would drink deep draughts and Law would be no more. The Master of the Dead would have the girl. She would serve him and remind him of beauty in a realm of zombies and shades. Beauty was his weakness, his perversion.

176805.overview:
Find the Lapora of Life. A brave knight without fear is the protagonist of this fantastic story set in the "Castle of Life". He will have to face a thousand dangers caused by the spirits, emissaries of the evil force, to be able to reach the magical Amphora of Life. Later, he will have to face other pitfalls before reaching the room of the evil one who has the power to turn into a monstrous dragon. If you come out victorious in the fight with the dragon, you can reach and save your beloved princess. Move as quickly as possible before someone notices a hostile presence in the room or kills you by throwing a huge boulder on your head. Don't waste your strength because you only have 4 lives available. Don't get distracted and always be ready with reflections!

An unofficial English translation was done by Hokuto Force on March 21, 2016.

176944.overview:
Very tough unofficial sequel created in SEUCK by Nik Townes & Markus (MTK). More refinement on the previously lost levels and better SEUCK tools were used to create this game. 
Several levels await your super-tough Commando in this vertical scrolling game. Armed with only a standard rifle and a few grenades you must take on hordes of Nazis. Some are wandering around in the open, while others have picked out hiding places, which you must approach from certain angles. Trees, rivers and bridges create a varied combat-like terrain and must be incorporated into your thinking. Extra grenades can be collected, and will definitely be required, as they allow you to kill from distance and thus avoid some enemy shots.

177174.overview: The second in the Crazy Dream Boulderdash series. A Boulder Dash style game where you have to dig through monster infested caves in search of diamonds. In each level you must collect a certain number of these diamonds, in order to open a portal to the next stage. Enemies can be squashed by falling boulders, which are released when the ground below them is removed or they are pushed onto empty ground, but be careful because these can also squash you. In later levels, difficulty is increased by many puzzle elements and shorter time limits.

177415.overview:
Shoikan\Crux is a game of logic that will not fail to thrill you. The concept is very simple: you have to arrange all the pieces on the screen so that at the end they are in the identical position (both in color and in place) to that indicated at the bottom. 

Published in both Magic Disk 64 1991/09 and in All C64 n.1 (1992/1993).

177618.overview: A "Commodore Home Planetarium" where you can learn about the stars. The magic of microelectronics has made it possible to have an accurate model of the universe in your own home at a modest cost. The awesome computations and enormous amounts of data are handled quickly and efficiently by your Commodore 64 computer. All you have to do is select your exploration commands and Sky Travel will return the information in pictorial form, directly on your screen - and in bright colors at that!

178418.overview: Chichén Itzá is a Spanish text-adventure, the final chapter of the Ci-U-Than trilogy of games. They all utilize the parser DAAD, that has capabilities similar to the Infocom Z-machine one (you can chain commands, correct misspellings, etc). This time the main quest is divided in two parts: In the first half you have to satisfy all the gods demands while exploring the ruined temple and solving its mystery. In the last part you journey from hell to heaven in an effort to liberate the god Kukulkán from his prison.

178419.overview:
The scene chosen for this adventure, the first one of the "Ci-U-Than" trilogy, is the Yucatan, a mysterious land in which legends say there are a lot of dangers, hidden treasures, unsolved mysteries, temples filled with traps... in short, the ingredients to which the good adventurer is used to deal with.

The adventure takes place on the island of Cozumel, where you must guide an archaeologist who had an incident. He was sailing towards it perfectly equipped, when an unfortunate shipwreck left him without anything. Do not think he only lost the map or the machete, no, he lost everything, including the trousers and the underclothes, reason why it's quite possible that an entrance in San Marcos, a coastal town near the place of the shipwreck, would carry serious problems with the justice. The main mission of the adventure is to discover all the hidden secrets of the island and then be able to escape from it.

178585.overview:
Try to make money at the stock market. Invest in stocks when their exchange price is low and when the price rises sell them to make profit.

You have $5000 in cash at the beginning of the game and 10 different securities to choose from.

179263.overview:
You are in the orbit of the moon of Geevor on your Comet Starfighter and your task is to protect its precious mines by finding and destroying as many Scavenger ships as possible during your watch. Although the Scavenger shuttles are difficult to locate, the infrared screen of your Comet will easily identify them, indicating your position in relation to them. You will have to approach the enemy at high speed, decreasing it you are in range to fire to increase accuracy. You have friends to help, remember that laser cannons are inactive against them. When comets approach you will need to dodge them to continue fighting.

Published in Italy as Comet Starfighter in Special PlayGames n.16 (marzo 1986).

179463.overview:
Earned 2nd place in the WiLD Demo Competition at Flashparty 2019. Commando 2084 is the mix between Commando and Robotron 2084: it is like the original Commando game, but using the Robotron 2084 controls.

Levels 2 and 3 have bosses (enemies taken from Robotron 2084)
The SFX used when these bossed are killed, are unused SFX from the original Commando.
Difficulty increased, otherwise the game would be too easy to play:
- No extra lives,
- 28 soldiers are inside forts, instead of 20.

179523.overview: Press the button/spacebar when the top color is the same as the bottom. Move up or down to change the top color. Doing it faster will give you more bonus points. The game is over when the time runs out.

179524.overview: An updated version of Frogger. More of Derek's rubbish for 2019. You must guide your frogs across the water, avoiding nasties and reaching each segment at the top to gain an ever high score.

179816.overview:
Published in Commodore Format 1994/04 (Issue #43) and released in the Power Pack as part of the "Shrewd Software Collection"

An Ikari Warriors themed SEUCK game developed by Martin Edwards.

180123.overview: One of several text-baed train management simulations from Dee-Kay Systems. This one was published in 1984. It was based on the Cornish Riviera Express, which is a British express passenger train that has run between London Paddington and Penzance in Cornwall since 1904.

180300.overview:
Carrun is a 1-2 player (co-operative) shmup developed by Codename Leslie using the Shoot 'Em Up Constructing Kit. The game is inspired by Death Race 2000.

The game was published in Floppy Magazine 1988/6.

180324.overview: A horizontally scrolling shoot 'em up that scrolls to the opposite side than usual. Created by Tommi Koistinen and released in Floppy Magazine 1988/6.

180830.overview:
Created by Terry Flynn, aka Roy Batty, this is an EXCELLENTLY done remake of the well-known star trek simulation. If you have already played the old sims, you already know how to play this one. there are subtle differences between this and those old originals. the game is played on a galactic grid of 8x9 sectors, each sector is cut into a grid of 8x8 parsecs, each parsec is 3.26 light years in size. The simulation begins as a large Klingon armada invades this galactic area...

You, Captain of the U.S.S. Enterprise, must defeat this invading force to save the Federation. There are 3 star bases within this galactic area where you can refuel and recharge the ships power and shields. You have short and long range sensors and unlimited photon torpedoes. In navigation .1 will move one parsec, .8 will move one full sector.  Good luck and God Speed!

181901.overview:
This version has only 2 of the 4 levels from the arcade game has simplistic graphics and came on cartridge and tape. In version 2 of the game was reissued on disk. The disk version has contemporary graphics and all four levels of the arcade game (Level 1 (v.1) = Level 1 (v.2), Level 2 (v.1) = Level 4 (v.2). The game principle of the two comparable levels has approx. stayed the same.

In Congo Bongo you take over the role of a jungle hunter who tries to catch a Gorilla named "Congo Bongo". In each of the two levels there are numerous perils between you and Congo in the shape of abysses, torrential rivers, falling coconuts, monkeys gone wild, snakes and rhinos. But hippos, huge piranhas and floating lily leaves will help in crossing the rivers and also monkeys that have taken a seat on your back can be shaken off again . . .

182005.overview:
A 2P Only (Simultaneous) sports style game. Here is a truly futuristic version of the football game. Invite a friend to challenge you in a space game whose end will be determined only by the expiration of time or by the exhaustion of the shots available to each player. Put yourself in the shoes of a goalkeeper driving a tank and get ready to defend your goal. Each player must try to hit the ball with the shots fired from the cannon, obviously directing it towards the opponent's goal. The task is not at all easy because the ball has to be hit with a graze to be able to move it from the center of the field. In fact, if you players hit it centrally, but from opposite sides, the ball would remain motionless until the blows of one of the players were exhausted. Have good fun figuring it out!

Published in Italy as Calcio Spaziale in New Special PlayGames n.50 (settembre 1992)  and in Hit Parade C64 n.71 (Ottobre 1992).

182159.overview:
Completely new graphics!
Here's a top quality release for you C64 owners as the C64 group Nostalgia has just released 'Commando Arcade SE, which is a special edition of their previous 2014 Commando Arcade remake of the classic game from the original way back in the early 80's. Although Commando was a great game on the C64, it could've been so much better, and thanks to Nostalgia they set out to re-release it as a faithful version to the Arcade and featured more levels, new level features, new graphics, a new scroller and much much more.

But this version goes even further! I thought the Commando Arcade release was the best 8-bit version of Commando by far, but with the new version released today I was proven wrong. Commando Arcade SE "IS" the  best version so far, A run and gun shoot em up that has lasted the ages has just got far far better and has pushed the boundary of greatness:

182184.overview: A homebrew fangame version of Boulderdash created by Cheech & Chong with 20 new caves to hurdle!

182187.overview: A set of 20 new caves from a true Boulderfreak who goes by the name Stormbringer.

182905.overview: The sequel and final game in the Cheech & Chong's boulder dash game set, a German homebrew fangame version of Boulderdash created by Cheech & Chong with 20 new caves to hurdle!

182909.overview: The second in the 7 part series of Crazy-Dash games by Germany's Stormbringer, containing 20 new Boulder Dash caves to mine.

182975.overview: Title Bout is an action-based boxing game for two players. Each player can play as a circa 1983 professional boxer, or as a historical great such as Muhammad Ali or Joe Louis. Each boxer has attributes for punching accuracy, defense, endurance, power, control, and others, which affect the outcomes of the matches, along with the fighting strategies you choose to employ.

183534.overview:
Cave Dave is a simple, but challenging monocrhomatic platformer for the C64. It was developed by Steve Engelhardt and published as a public domain game in 1984.

The goal of each level is to collect all the treasure and then rescue your older brother at the top of the screen. Good luck!

184134.overview: Written in BASIC v2 and compiled, this game by Felice Nardella aka Kimono pits you against the COVID 9, socially distance yourself from that baddy!

184251.overview: Trivia: Science aka CompuQuiz - Science. A trivia quiz focused on Science and nature.

185127.overview: It's thermonuclear war! Break the computer code to launch your missiles, then guide your interceptors before enemy missiles converge with your cities. This is a game in two parts. The first part plays a lot like a sliding block puzzle. You are given a figure in a 3 x 3 grid to match. Using the joystick and fire button, you rotate pieces in a larger grid to try to match the smaller figure. If you do that, you can select a missile launch site. Eventually, the enemy will launch its own missiles. You position your crosshair at the radar dot for the enemy missile, and can then launch an intercepter. This part of the game is more action-oriented as you "fly" your intercepter to take down the enemy nuke

186582.overview: City of Atlantis is a text adventure developed by Clive Gifford and Robert Young and published as a type-in program in their book Creating Adventures on Your Commodore 64 by Interface Publications in 1984. You start in the Atlantean detention area and must get out, find diving gear and escape the airlock and reach the surface.

187352.overview:
Copter Duel is yet another two-player only vehicle vs. vehicle (in this case helicopters) shoot 'em up for the C64. As with all games of this nature, whoever has the most "kills" is the overall winner. You each have three helicopters each.

This game was developed by Ronald Mayer and published by Tronic Verlag GmbH in Compute mit 1988/03.

187579.overview:
A puzzle game in the vein of Drelbs that was published by Go Games n.11 (July / August 1986) as Change also published under the name Square.

In an intricate maze of revolving doors, chased by one or more guardians, you must try to compose as many squares as possible. In these squares you will occasionally see the access door to another game phase or the possibility of accessing higher difficulty levels, but be careful, because in addition to all this you may find yourself facing a certain death or the risk of ending up imprisoned with no possibility of salvation. Move fast and try to be smarter than your enemies.

187764.overview:
Diamond Drop is a  variation of the old Atari Arcade game Avalanche. It is keyboard controlled only. This game was developed by Eric Brandon and published by COMPUTE! Publicatins, Inc. in COMPUTE! 1983/09 (Issue #40), as well as COMPUTE!'s First Book of C64 Games

It was also released by Alpha Software Ltd. and released in Europe under the name Collection Day and published as part of "The Big One" Collection. 

Also released in Norway under the name Diamant Slipp by Data-Tronic

187851.overview:
Single player vs computer implementation of chess released as part of "Board Games" game pack named as Chess there and also in SYS PD Diskett#30 (1992).

Also released in Published as part of the "75 Spill Datatronic" compilation in Germany. As well as in Italy by WizardSoft and in the UK by Alpha Software Ltd. under the simple title "Chess"

190509.overview:
Caveman is an unofficial adaptation of the Grandstand/Tomy/Tandy electronic table-top game. It was written as an exercise in learning 6502 assembler. In this game you are a caveman who needs to steal dinosaur eggs without getting caught. Played on a single screen shown from a side view, the caveman is controlled directly. Eggs regularly appear below on a dinosaur on the right side of the screen. The caveman needs to move right, grab an eggs and bring it back to the cave to score points. Eggs cannot be stolen while the dinosaur is looking. An axe can be thrown to stun it temporarily. 

The caveman also needs to avoid dino fire. A pterodactyl will also appear attempting to steal eggs from the cave. It can be killed by throwing an axe. Eggs need to be collected before they hatch. There are multiple levels and the game keeps track of the score. Extra lives can be earned at every 2,000 points. There are two difficulty levels. Visually the game recreates the large multi-coloured display recognisable from the Grandstand tabletops.

192098.overview: It is time to save the world. This is a game in which requires your C64's keyboard. The aim of the game is to try to save the world from a major catastrophe by guessing the correct number. You have a set time to take a guess. The computer will let you know whether or not you are too high or too low or guessed correctly. For each correct guess, you will score bonus points. As each level progresses the game will become much harder.

192349.overview: A casino gambling game released by Bug-Byte and in Italy's Go Games n.15 (December 1986) and in Alga Soft n.2b.

194072.overview:
Try to outwit your computer with this fast, multi-level chess program whose intelligence routines are written entirely in machine language. There are versions for the Commodore 64; VIC-20 with at least 8K memory expansion; Ataris with at least 32K RAM; and Apples with at least 48K RAM and a disk drive. All versions  except Apple require a joystick.

The game is single-player, but also has a computer vs. computer demo mode.

Released in COMPUTE! 1984/12 (Issue #55), Best of COMPUTE! & Gazette, and COMPUTE!'s Commodore Collection - Vol.2

194302.overview: The Noun is an educational game that tests the user on his/her knowledge of nouns in their various forms. It was developed by published by Micro-Ed, Inc. in 1982.

194923.overview:
You are the pilot of a new spaceship. You must tet the craft to its limits. You can fly along the canyon and through the space maze. The ship will change color to warn of changes in the canyon size. At teh end of your flight you will be ranked. You must not hit the sides of the canyon, but asteroids will fly by. Good luck! 
 
 
Published as part of the "Star Fighter" game pack, COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1984/01 (Issue #07) / no definite name, game says "64-Canyon".

195673.overview:
Are you sitting comfortably? Then I'll begin. It's Christmas Eve and Santa's reindeer have gone missing- they sneaked out whilst he was reading Commodore User. So the silly old Duffer's got to go out and find them, leaving you to deliver all the presents on his spare (battery operated) sleigh.

But the presents are located in the maze, and they're guarded by ice demons. Your job is to steer your way through the maze and collect them, whilst zapping the demons. Not having Duracells, the sleigh tends to sink of its own accord so you need to use its 'snow thrusters' to gain height. You'll get extra lives on completing the 2nd, 4th and 6th screens and you get more points for picking up sacks of presents further down the screen. By the way, you'll need a joystick (in port 2) for this one. The controls are: Joystick left move left Joystick right-move right Joystick down fire snow bullets Fire button-fire snow thrusters.

 Published in Commodore User 1986/12.

195696.overview: The age old board game of Checkers or Droughts. Published in COMPUTE! 1983/05 (Issue #36) and as a game of "The Big 100" collection.

196684.overview: A space platformer game by Marc E.H. Dawson & Robert W. Tinman that takes place in the Caves of Venus, naturally. It has a relationship with The Nodes of Yesod, which wasn't programmed by Robert W. Tinman, but the sequel Arc of Yesod was, though CSDB shows that The Nodes of Yesod was an update over Caves of Venus, Yesod was published before the release of this game. This is possible as release could be years after creation but it is interestingly circuitous and publication is always another layer of complication and can take much longer.

196685.overview:
The 4th sample game from The Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit by Sensible Software
Created with the Kit by Gary Penn & Gary Liddon.

196795.overview: A ROM hack of the original Championship Sprint overhead racing game for 1 to 3 players with added tracks released by Myth in 1993.

197027.overview:
A  puzzle game by Charles Grey's Iceout Games.

Released on May 13, 2011.

197352.overview: Count 'em (also known as CMA-2: Count 'em) is a simple counting game from children. The year of release is currently unknown. It was developed and released by Micro-Ed, Inc. Kindergarten and 1st grade focus. The learner counts  from one to ten steam locomotives on the computer screen.

198452.overview:
Chessboard Nim is a mathematical puzzle game played on a board resembling a chess or checker board. It was published as a type-in program in the 1983 book  "Games Commodore 64 Computers Play"

It was also released in The Netherlands under the name Schaakbord Nim in the Dutch version of the book, which was titled "Het Commodore 64 Computer-Spelen Boek" which came out a year later.

198677.overview: Crush is a side-scrolling shooter that has some similarities games like R-Type. It was developed by André Bürger and published by Smash Designs. The preview version was also published in GO64! 1999/06.

198813.overview:
No to be confused with the ZX Spectrum game of the same name, this game is a vertically scrolling shooter developed by C.P. and J.J. Gosoen using Chris Yates' Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit.  It was released into the public domain in 1988. In Italy, it was released under the name Bruffer in Special C64 n.4 (1991/1992) and as Cingo in Special Program n.92 (dicembre 1992). 
 
ON the moon of Cingo 12 of the XMT 125484 galaxy, the longest and most horrible war in recorded history is taking place. You are a solider of the Green army and with your tracked vehicle you are able to venture inside enemy lines to destroy as many of the enemy as possible. Use your protonic cannon and avoid as many enemy shots as you can. Beware, their goal is to annihilate you!

199524.overview: Very nice gambling game where you can play from 0 to 5 with or without the participation of the computer player, who you can have play with himself if you like, he sure likes it. Published in Hebdogiciel Hors Serie N°2, and Hebdogiciel Software N°6.

199955.overview: Computershop is a German language business simulation in which you have to run and operate a computer store. This game was developed by Martin Arnold and published by Tower Software in 1986.

200036.overview:
Candle Burner is a fun little timed Christmas themed game in which your goal is to light all the candles on a Christmas tree in an attempt to get on the top 5 "Burners" list by beating one of the top five scores. Once you light one candle, you must return to the base candle to light your match again.

The game was released as part of the RGCD C64 16KB Cartridge Game Development Competition 2013.

201896.overview:
Copy-Cat!! is a game similar to Simon, and is a clone of a similar game of the same name that was released on the VIC-20. It was developed by John Dale in 2020 as part of the Cassette 50 Charity Competition.

The game is actually a clone of a VIC-20 type-in game of the same name.

202197.overview:
A ROM HACK of Shaun Southern's Cosmic Causeway: Trailerblazer II with modified physics and levels, done by Gollum and released in 1987. 
 
The hack was made to play more closely to the original C16/Plus4 version as the C64 port was kind of buggy. The hack also features 24 additional levels.

202932.overview:
Psytronik Software presents a debut C64 release from Stephan Katteneder with music by Saul Cross.

While away your coffee breaks by blasting the birdies as they majestically flap their way across the screen in this fun target-shooter.  Line up your cross-hair sights and get your timing right - or the bird will mock you and fly away to survive another day.  Try to beat your last score before the timer - or your coffee break runs out!
The Coffee Break Shootout  
  
** FEATURES **
 
· Superbly animated birdies to blast
 
· Nicely drawn seasonal backdrops
 
· 1351 Mouse support
 
· Catchy soundtracks
 
· PAL & NTSC compatible

This game was released in a double pack along with Total Refill.

203477.overview:
An early Cute-em'up vertically scrolling shooter created by Emiliano Sciarra. He writes about the game: Back in 1986, I designed several videogames on paper, without actually programming them -- I was only 14 then and I knew BASIC only. One of them was a scrolling shoot'em up starring a cute little dog (dubbed "Ciuffy" after one of my sister's most beloved peluche) escaping from the city whose inhabitants ruled against animals. His main weapon were his barks (or, as we say in Italy, "BAU"), while his enemies were all sorts of citizens either on foot or on cars, motorbikes, automatic dog-catchers, farm tractors, roadrollers etc. The more fierce the opponent, the more BAUs were required to send him off.

Two years later, I got SEUCK and was immediately fascinated by this impressive software. After just days I was, rather unexpectedly, working on "Ciuffy", whose design was almost perfect for such a construction kit. I worked alone, as many programmers then: I did all in the game, from the graphics to the sound effect -- and while I am quite proud of the "BAU" sound, the fact I was not a graphic artist shows in several rough and sketchy parts.

I put all together very quickly, and after about two weeks the game was ready. The game was intended just to get in touch with the basic SEUCK routines (that is why some details are not very refined), but the final result was quite good and entertaining, so I tried to send it to one of the publishing company in Italy accepting games from independent programmers: Systems Editoriale, which at the same time was printing the notorious (in Italy) "Commodore Computer Club" magazine. Very unexpectedly, the magazine director liked the game and decided to release it in one of their monthly cassette-only periodical, "Software Club", as the opening game, the very same year.

203478.overview:
Touted as being harder than the original Elite release. This version was released in Italy as Missione Commando in Supplementi Edigamma/pubblirome - big 100 (1987), in Special Games n.16 (settembre 1988), and in Super C64 e C128 n.21 (marzo 1988). Also released in Stonysoft #0291 / a.k.a. "Commando III".  

A vertically scrolling shooter created with the Shoot'em Up Construction Kit. Inspired by those films that tell the stories of reckless soldiers who go alone behind enemy lines with the task of creating confusion through destruction and killing. The hero must survive and kill as many of the enemy as possible. They are aided by the cover of rocks and other impediments while our hero has no such luxury.

203754.overview: Clue is a homebrew adaptation of the board game Clue. Solve the mystery by finding the killer, the weapon and the place of murder.

203755.overview: Clue! is another conversion of the classic board game Clue/Cluedo. Like in the original, three cards are randomly selected showing the murderer, the weapon and the room where the crime happened. The objective is to deduct these cards by moving between rooms, making accusations and analyzing the information gathered. The game was developed by Joe Obrin originally as a gift for his wife. However it eventually made its way into the public domain.

204183.overview:
Colorbot (also known as Robotattack) is a game similar in some ways to Robotron: 2084, but using only one joystick. This was developed by Kevin Martin in 1983 and published in the following:

• North America: COMPUTE! 1984/01 (Issue #44)
• Italy: Super VIC & C64 A1-N2 (July/August 1984)
• Courbois Software also released a Dutch language version as well.

Only the Dutch conversion has a title screen.

A version for the VIC-20 was also available in the same issue of COMPUTE!

205093.overview:
Cricket's Revenge is a simple collect 'em up in which you play the last surviving cricket on Earth. Collect as much fruit from the evil Farmer Jones' farm before the time runs out. Avenge your fellow crickets who were killed off by Jones.

Developed by Joylon West and published in PCW 1985.04.18 (Vol 4 No 16)

205375.overview: Charlie Deus is an Italian language text adventure game for the C64. It was released by Systems Editoriale s.r.l. in 1986. The game's author/coder is currently unknown.

205428.overview: This is a top-down racing game for one or two players. Select the racing course you wish to participate in a big race. You can either race against the computer or a friend. Try to control your car wisely using the UP control on a joystick. The game has additional options in which will enhance play slightly. Can you become one of the top racers through all 8 courses, or will you retire to the pit?

205431.overview: Charles Bryan: Prigioniero del Futuro (translates to Charles Bryan: Prisoner of the Future) is an Italian language graphic text adventure game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Bonaventura Di Bello and published in Explorer No.10 (09/1987).

205433.overview: Chaos in Space is a fixed-screen shooter similar to Space Invaders, only without the shields to protect you from the enemy fire. It was developed by Paul Williams and published in Commodore Disk User 1988/03-04.

205434.overview: CharSnake 64 is a snake clone developed by Michele Zuccalà and released to the public domain in 2020. It's called CharSnake 64 because it uses character graphics, rather than sprites.

205436.overview: Two teenagers get up one morning, after playing a whole weekend of Grand Theft Auto (could replace with similar game/genre). Easily influenced, they decide to go for a street race, but realise quickly they don't have a car. Not to let this deter them, and fueled with 48 hours non-stop GTA and not pleased with the fact that it is a Monday morning. They get on their bikes and go for a ride... Warning: Remember kids, never go on a bike ride when you're in a bad mood.

205459.overview:
Deep in the underground catacombs are huge, gleaming treasure boxes that seem to be just waiting for a new owner. However, beware: It is said that they are busy with the magic of the great Zambalo, which is full of diamonds, goblets and pearls. It is certainly not good-natured magic!

The legends also tell that deep in the dark corridors and caves are slumbering even more valuable treasure chests with an unspeakably precious treasure ...

205906.overview:
The Cold Shower is a pinball game developed by Charles M. Duncan using Olaf Lubeck's Pinabll Construction Set. It was released in the following:

-   Pcs Club Disk #07
-   Stonysoft #1730

206201.overview: Cosmic Killer is a Danish language fixed screen shooter in the same vein as games like Space Invaders and Galaxian. It was coded entirely in BASIC by Niels Lausten and published as a type-in listing in SOFT Special #85/1 (January 1985)

206202.overview: CovidBreaker is a public domain homebrew game developed for the Commodore 64 by Davide Fichera and released as part of the 2020 BASIC 10Liner Contest. It is a collect 'em up and a clone of the old Sierra On-Line game Jawbreaker, except instead of Jawbreaker candy, you have to compete with covid spores.

206367.overview:
Critical Mass is a two player only public domain board game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Jim Tu and Jaggy Tu. The year of release is currently unknown.

Game description:

Critical Mass is a two player board game based on a little known board game called Explosion.

You are presented with a 6x6 grid. Each player in turn places one of his counters (either an 0 or an X) into an empty square, or a square already occupied by one or more of his OWN counters.

However, each square has a point at which critical mass is reached and fission occurs. Corner squares explode when two counters are on them, side squares explode when containing three counters, and central squares go up when four counters occupy their space.

When an explosion occurs, the counters on the exploding square are distributed into the adjacent squares. Any enemy counters on the latter squares are captured and become counters belonging to the mover. Should receiving squares attain critical mass, further explosions will result.

The player having no counters left at the end of his opponent's move is the loser.

206655.overview:
Attack chopper vs the aliens. This shooter was created by Mike Sedore and published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1986/08 (Issue #38), and much later re-published in GO64! 2003/01. Only quick maneuvering and accurate firing can save the day in this fast-action, arcade-style game. 

As the sole trained pilot for the army's top-secret "Chopper 1," an attack helicopter equipped with a powerful pulse laser, you're sent to defend your city when it's suddenly invaded by aliens. The city's other defense is a glowing force field which hovers above the skyline. The alien's spaceship passes back and forth over the city while continually dropping bombs which gradually blast their way through the force field and, eventually, into the city itself. The bombs will also 
destroy your chopper if contact is made. You've been sent to destroy the bombs with Chopper I's laser before they reach the city. The alien's spacecraft is made of an indestructible alien alloy, and it's invulnerable to your laser blasts. It will, however, destroy you if you get in its path.

206657.overview:
An arcade platformer of the most basic type, created by Steven R. McCloskey and published first in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1985/11 (Issue #29) and then later as part of the Street Games published "Red Pack" in Australia and New Zealand. Children will enjoy netting the chicken in this action game for the 64, VIC, Plus/4, and C16.

You're equipped with a net and a pair of good, strong legs. And you'll need them in "Chicken Catcher." The object of the game is to catch a falling chicken in your net by timing your jump as you leap from one platform to another. The more 
chickens caught, the more points you collect. Fowl Play, for sure!

206663.overview:
An election strategy game that came out in time for the 1984 Election in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1984/08 (Issue #14), then in the Best of COMPUTE! & Gazette, and later in COMPUTE!'s Commodore 64 & 128 Collection. This two-player national 
election simulation ranks as one of the best games we've published. With the right 
strategy, your candidate can make it to the White House.

206935.overview: Keplero (also known as Caverne 2) is a "lander" game from Italy for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Alberto Facchini and published in Next Game #03 (03/1985)

207115.overview: Caveman is a single-screen, single player platformer where your goal is to either avoid or beat the attacking dinosaurs and ptetosaurs with your trusty bat. It was originally published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1990/11.

207116.overview:
Crown No.1 is a 1984 German language video slot machine simulation for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Claus Vigelius & Ralf Gutjahr and published in 64'er 1984/07 [Extraprogramm auf Kassette]. This program was written for all those who want to try a slot machine without investing a lot of money. Crown No. I simulates the slot machine of the same name in the inns and arcades. A corresponding graphic was achieved using sprites and self-defined characters. Crown No. 1 asks you after the start how much capital you want to invest. You can replace up to 30 marks. Then you have to wait a while, the characters will be redefined.  
 
The aim of the game is to get three matching symbols in the five windows. Once this has been achieved, there are several possibilities. Three crowns result in special games. In special games, each win is increased to three marks, each golden field in the middle is counted as a win (three marks). The number of special games is determined by pressing a button while the selection is running. Everything is presented visually. When the starter lights up, the selection can be restarted for a specific time.  The crown in the middle window acts as a wild card for any amount. A crown alone wins 30 pfennigs.

207443.overview: In this game you have been pulled into a crazed musical world that really doesn't like you for some reason. There are gnashing teeth, and flying pianos coming at you from all sides that really want to do you harm. Thankfully there are good things in this world as musical notes are there to help, collect enough of them and you'll finally be able to kill at least one of those menacing mouths and make the game that bit easier!

207521.overview:
A single button game for Commodore 64. Our friend will have to dodge different obstacles during his ride on an electric skateboard.

Game developed entirely in assembly language with CBM prg Studio.

PATAGONIA's first game, and many more to come.

Cabygame: 

- 7 speeds
- 4 bonuses
- 1 slowdown
- 4 seasons: summer, autumn, winter and spring
- 1 end at 9999 points.
- Clouds & Sun

Every 100 points, the distance between obstacles is reduced. It is notable at 5000 points or from 8000 points you will have a horde of obstacles!

The item "Slow" reduces the speed by one point. Maybe it is more necessary when you are at full speed, and you can avoid it when you are at low speed :)

207522.overview: A war strategy game created by Eugen Traeger and published as part of the "64'er Lern-Spiele" sample disk which was included in 64'er 07/1993 / a.k.a. "Castle Wars".

207749.overview: The game is a sort of Space Invaders clone with a twist. The invaders are not invading, but are trying to rescue their criminal friends locked up in a prison at the centre of the screen, and you must prevent them from doing so. Thanks to contributor Alan B, we have learnt that it was originally based on the 1979 coin-op Cosmic Guerilla by Universal.

207994.overview:
Crazy Man is an Italian language single-screen platformer for one player. In the game, you play a blue man who has to collect little miniature cyan colored "women" while avoiding the enemy that is floating around the screen.

The game was developed by Luigi Recanatese, but the year of release is currently unknown.

208094.overview: Carrot Juggler is a 1-4 player pinball for the C64 using the C64 version of Olaf Lubeck's Pinball Construction Set. It was developed in 1991 by Ronald B. Rome. Released as part of Pcs Club Disk #27.

208119.overview: Chiappucci Pizza Service is a 1992 German language public domain business simulation (in this case a pizza parlor) for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Peter Diehm and released by his PDPD Software label.

208232.overview:
Castle of Spirits is a 1988 text adventure by Anthony Maro for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Anthony Maro and published in the following:

•   Loadstar #056
•   Digital Talk #003 (26.09.1993)

A text adventure intended to help you learn techniques you can use in your own programs. The Castle of Spirits is a small interactive adventure game which has most of the features you're accustomed to in text games. You use verb-noun commands like "Go House" or "Take Box". If you want to take a two-word noun, such as an oil can take the second word, eg. "Take Can".  Normal shorthand such as N, S, E, W for the cardinal directions, U and D can be used for up and down.  
 
You are in a large courtyard with a dilapidated shed in the corner. The south edge is lined by an old stone wall with a portcullis in the middle. Whilst going about your business a more than slightly deranged apparition appears. He seems to be creaming some nonsense about no escape. The ghost very impolitely laughs in your face and then vanishes to whatever unsightly place he appeared from. You will need to prepare to take on all the horrors a gothic castle can dish out and if you are lucky, you may get out of this castle alive!

208432.overview:
Chess Board is a very simplistic 2 player only implementation of chess for the Commodore 64. Instead of standard chess pieces, it just uses text abbreviations to represent the pieces. 

It was developed by P.E. Sullivan & J. Sawczak and published by Commodore Educational Software in 1983.

208436.overview:
Not to be confused with the game from CP Verlag of the same name, Chicago is a crosshair shooter developed by Bombjack Ltd. using the Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit. It was released to the public domain in 1988.

The game takes place during the Al Capone era of Chicago. Shoot and kill the mobsters in the building before they shoot and kill you.

208437.overview:
Children Dash 1 (also known as Children 1) is a 1988 Boulder Dash game made by Boulderwilli using Jeffrey Schneider's Boulder Dash Construction Set. 

It was called Children Dash 1 because Boulderwilli aimed to gear the game toward a younger audience.

It was released as a "Christmas" release, so sometime around late November to late December of 1988.

208439.overview:
The Chinese Box Mystery is a text adventure for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Tony Rome and released into the public domain in 2012.

Story:

It was spring and you pondered previous events. It was your incompetence that had led to the theft of a Chinese box. In the box was a map showing the location of a unclear device set to detonate!

Zhuang Shen, a crazed scientist, had sent the box to you with a note which read "If you can open the box you may prevent a great disaster. Failure to open it correctly will release a deadly nerve gas."

You no longer have the box, which was stolen by Lei Feng, your arch enemy, who was last seen in Hong Kong. You must find him and the box before time runs out! Good luck!

208521.overview:
An update to the original 1985 OziSoft release of the game. This brings thing up to date, 90's style with all new questions and updated answers. 

 It is a game where you move around the game board based on correct answers trivia questions, a non-trivial pursuit by my estimation. The game board is a set of shoals your game boat token must move around and place over the fish to win.

208532.overview:
The New Dimension, in co-op with Alf Yngve are both proud to present Cosmic Combat Deluxe. A fun arcade blaster for one or two players. This game was originally created and designed using the Shoot Em Up Construction Kit and has been majorly transformed into the SEUCK Redux engine. It was published in the Reset 64 #14 Mix-i-Disk. 

Your mission is to fly into the deep void of infinite space and fight your way against fleets of assorted alien invaders. Each alien has its own behaviour patterns.

Look out for bonus stages and of course alien boss waves.

You will gain an extra ship for every 10,000 points scored.

The latest version is version 1.1, which was released on January 9, 2022.

208570.overview:
A junior edition version created using the Crillion Construction Set by Oliver Kirwa & Andreas Kwias with music by Otto Järvinen. Like the original the game is similar to Breakout except there is no paddle and the player controls the ball directly. The ball always bounces up and down and the player only controls its horizontal movement. When the ball hits a block of the same color it will dissolve. The ball can change color when hitting a color changer blocks, marked with an asterisk. The object of the game is to clear all blocks while avoiding the skull blocks.

When the player hits a skull block, a life is lost and the level restarts, resetting any progress made so far in that level. There also are unbreakable walls and slider blocks. The slider blocks can only be moved around when the ball has the same color.

208640.overview: An update to Championship Lode Runner made by 808 and Browny of the The A-Team using the Lode Runner Construction Kit and inspired by the music of the time; New Order, Tears for Fears and Prince.

208793.overview:
Club Squash is a simple single-player keyboard controlled Breakout clone for the Commodore 64 that uses character graphics rather than sprites.

The game was developed by Robert Young and published in as a type-in program in the book "More Games for Your Commodore 64" in 1984.

208866.overview:
Collins is a solitaire variant. It was developed by Maurice Jones and published in Loadstar #105 in 1993.

COLLINS is played for score. Points are made by correctly identifying each card of the deck as a red spot card, a red face card, a black spot card, or a black face card. Use the CRSR keys to set the pointer to your choice and RETURN to select.

If the choice is correct, the card will be turned and played face up by Suit. If the choice is wrong, a BUZZ is heard, and you must try again.

When the game begins, 166 tries are available. If all cards are identified in the available tries, a bonus and an  additional life are awarded, the deck is Shuffled, and additional tries are added to the number left.

At each level, the bonus and the award per card and increased, but the number of the additional tries is decreased. If the deck is not exhausted in the allotted tries, a life is lost, and you must attempt the level again if you have any lives left. The game ends when all lives are lost.

208867.overview: Code Name Eagle II is a vertically scrolling shooter for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Kille the Killer & Mas the Great  using Chris Yates' Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit. It was released into the public domain in 1988.

209206.overview: Ferry skiers across the gap on 3 levels. You can only lose so many and your days of skyway transport will be cut short. Published in Software Club N°19 and as Cabs in Commodore Club - software # 19 and in Hit Parade C64 n.37 (Settembre 1989).

209254.overview: In this crosshair game you are attending the Shooting Range with City backgrounds. In first-person view you should move the aim and shoot different items (cars, dinos, targets, dogs, etc.) moving on the three stages. You have 50 bullets, and each successful hit will give you a certain number of points and speed up the current item on the stage. Published in Commodore 64 Club #03 [Italian Release] / made with "The Games Creator".

209702.overview:
Crossfire Canyon is a 1-2 (NOT co-op) player arcade game for the Commodore 64.

The player controls a small character who can move horizontally about the center of the level. On either side is an erupting volcano, from which creatures appear, and stack on top of each other. The creatures will shoot rocks at the character. If the character is hit, they lose a life. Otherwise, the player can pick up the missed rock, and throw it back at the creature. The strength of the thow is dependent upon how long the throw button is pressed. If a creature is struck, they are removed from the level. The player wins by clearing a level of creatures. The player starts with 3 lives, and it's game over when all are lost.

209758.overview:
Chiller 2 by Cosine Systems is a multi-level single-screen platform game inspired by the Mastertronic game Chiller.

The aim of the game is to collect 20 crosses on each level while avoiding all sorts of nasty ghouls, witches, and critters that drain your energy when you make contact with them. While you’re at it, make sure you also look out for where you stand as each level is littered with poisonous mushrooms that will also result in a loss of energy.

There are 12 challenging creepy levels for you to complete so I hope you are not afraid of the dark.

210241.overview: Except for the new level design, there are no further differences to the original game Crillion. With the help of the joystick a ball is controlled, that can be recolored over color blocks and as in Breakout resolve stones of the same color. Furthermore there are push-able stones that pose unwanted obstacles and skull fields that cost a life. Already the first levels have a relatively high difficulty level and without strategy probably no level can be solved. Game was published in 64'er Sonderheft 85.

210242.overview: The easy to use editor of the original "Crillion" led to some more or less official (like Crillion II) and home-made sequels, which are nothing more than a bundle of fresh levels created by Oliver Kirwa and published in 64'er Sonderheft 54.

210297.overview:
It is the year 2072.  

A giant asteroid was heading towards planet earth. During that event, a special rescue operation was taking place. The Interspace Legion has transported good people to the neighboring planet “Mars”. People were able to live there as a temporary settlement until a new suitable planet was found. The remaining people, the bad people, were all left to perish back on Earth. They were being punished for the crimes they committed towards humanity, the environment and animal cruelty. After the asteroid impact, Earth was now deemed to be uninhabitable. 

Inside a Space Lab down on Mars, Scientists made an amazing discovery, a brand-new green and blue planet. Intrigued to find out more about the planet, the scientists sent out a drone. It was discovered that the planet contained oxygen, gas and water and was a perfect match for humanity to evolve even further. The planet was named EarthX (Earth 10) 

The Interspace Legion trained many pilots and sent them to transport people from “Mars” to “EarthX” (Earth 10) via Cruiser-X starships. The special operation was becoming successful. That was, until the ships were on their way back to Mars. Fleets of alien bases mysteriously appeared, and then shot the Interspace Legion’s Cruiser-X ships down.  

Nobody survived, except for you, the pilot of Cruiser-X 79. Instead, you get pulled into a prison base, where your ship was captured with you inside it. You attempt to hack into the alien base using the supercomputer on board your starship. It releases the cargo bay doors, and you fly for freedom. - That was until the aliens spotted you. Now they are out to stop you. 

Not only do you have an escape mission. You also have a big battle for survival in your hands.

210364.overview:
The story: You are Sparlok, the warrior wizard. Mage of the 33rd degree to the counsil of the Morning Star, Royal astronomer to King Hegel Pemborg I and keeper of the magical staff of Pleaedes. Now the kingdom of Toëffelbard has been overrun by the forces of the dark light. It is your task to restore order to the realm and to vanquish the Nine of Wormwood. Along the way you will have to battle undead skeletons, black scorpions, witches and other nasties. There is also a dragon that bars your way to victory. You will also pass by the magic tree of the 'knowledge of that which you don't know you know' (Isilmivtenib) and the river of blood. Slog your way through the Castle complex and eventually good shall triumph... well maybe.

The game was made using the Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit.

210370.overview: Not to be outdone the C64 has also had some new games to play this week, as we've also learnt from Saberman that Protovision have released a very early teaser of a game called ' Cow & Chicken '. Now unlike the other games we've mentioned, this alpha download is purely to demonstrate the new player control system and movement engine, although you can select each character and view the different screens in the game itself.

210372.overview:
Genesis Project proudly presents a new game for your favourite computer: C=Rex Offline - A C64 adaptation of the popular Chrome offline T-rex game. We released it at Datastorm in Gothenburg (We handed out 40 copies on disk too). Coded by Wertstahl, idea and testing by hedning, and music by our great friend LFT. Enjoy! 

release party : Datastorm Summer 2017

210787.overview: Commie UFO Attack is a fixed screen shooter in which you control a tank on the bottom of the screen and must blast away at the space "commies". The game was developed by Kenneth Burrell and Steve Goldsmith. The release type is NOT currently known,

211323.overview: Climber is a 1983 C64 game heavily inspired by the arcade game Crazy Climber. It was developed by Australian based coder Terry Mason and originally published by Computer Classics Pty. It was later released in Europe a year later, however the publisher is not known, and the name was changed to Ape Escape.

213282.overview: This game is an entry in the 2022 Reset64 4KB Craptastic Game Competition, it is a big rhythm shooter in a small package.

213284.overview: A challenging arcade action game in which you need to surround each of the stars in a Tron like way to complete the stage. In this game from Inufoto, your task as the wood-be hero, is to traverse around the screen while avoiding monsters to collect as many stars as possible to win the game. What makes this different other than just picking the stars up, is not only can your character use a trail around each collectable star with the more stars you collect in one go the higher your score, but the trail can also be used to block the monster making life a little bit easier for you!

213298.overview: Corner Man is a single player grid capture game similar to games like Crush Roller and Amidar from Italy for the Commodore 64. It was published by Edisoft S.r.l. in Next Game #08 (05/1986). The game's actual coder is currently unknown.

213358.overview: Catch a Byte to Eat is a simple Snake game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Bruce Beck. The year of release is not currently known.

213359.overview:
In this game you have to well, catch a little white bouncing ball. You control a tire or donut shaped sprite. The goal is to catch the ball directly in the center of the player sprite by pressing the fire button. You cannot move while the fire button is pressed down.

This game was developed by Tobias Gohlke (also known as Toggle) for the Commodore 64 Crap Game Compo 2006 (C64CGC).

213424.overview:
Coball is a single player vertically scrolling shoot 'em up for the Commodore 64. It was developed by R. Aldridge & N. Cusworth using the Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit and published in the following:

-   Commodore Disk User 1989/09-10
-   Your Commodore 1991/04 (Issue #16)

213645.overview: Not to be confused with the Electric Dreams game of the same name, this is a variant of the cult favorite solitaire card game of the same name. This was developed by Maurice Jones and released in Loadstar #108 in 1993.

213727.overview: The game is similar to the first Cizzy Doo, except in this game you gather bombs instead of keys. The game was developed by Roland Kunz and published by BB Software in 1994.

213728.overview:
Clash of Wills is a World War II strategy game for the Commodore 64 for up to 2 players. It was developed by Marc Summerlott and published by Digital Kamp Group (DKG) in 1985.

It is based on the "what if" scenario, if the Western Allies went to war with the Soviet Union.

214164.overview: Canadair is an Italian language Bomber/Blitz clone for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Jean-François Séhan and published as a type-in game in the book "Supergiochi per il Commodore 64" in 1985.

214271.overview: Castle Climber is a Midieval themed Crazy Climber clone for the Commodore 64. It was developed and released by Nello Galiano on March 12, 2022 as part of a Crazy Climber challenge competition.

214332.overview: Cyforce 1 (also known as Cyforce One) is a single player shooter for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Alf Yngve and released by Binary Zone PD in 1992.

214653.overview:
Join a sequence of at least two adjacent circles of the same colour to clear them and score points, the more are cleared in one move the more you score.  

Cleared circles will be replaced by new colours dropping from the top. You can move around corners to create L, S or U shapes, however you can't move back on yourself to draw a T-shape for example.

You have 90 seconds to build as high a score as possible.

As with my other entry it will only be playable in the browser until the competition deadline passes. Programmed in BASIC on TheC64.

Developed by Nick "Arlasoft" Sherman as part of the Cassette 50  Charity Competion in 2020.

214957.overview:
Part of the Commodore 64 project by Chessforeva featuring a number of chess puzzles published in print in 1994 (1994 Konemann, Laszlo Polgar). 

   306  checkmates in 1 move
   3391 checkmates in 2 move
   743  checkmates in 3 move

 User can solve them one by one.

214958.overview: Originally intended to be a shooter with 2D scrolling, this was created as a preview of work done, but it never got past this point in development, so currently it is a action game where you avoid collisions, but not much else.

214959.overview: A remake of the Melbourne House Castle of Doom (or the Courbouis Software Dutch version if you prefer, which itself was from the book "Commodore 64 Games Book". In 2017 it was dusted off and updated by Marco Pistorio and Esteban Palladino. Like the original you can explore the rooms within the castle walls, look for treasure and try to avoid the slime monsters and killer robots. Points are gained by moving over question marks and killing monsters or robots with your Proton gun. As you move off the screen from one room you are presented with another. Move back and you return to the same room but now with different contents! You are killed if you touch the electrified walls or any of the monsters. Some monsters are faster than others and the robots are very dangerous.

214960.overview:
Chobin, a very good sailor, went to the seashore every morning to breathe int the good sea air, always immersed in his thoughts, he would never have imagined that one day he would have to face risks and dangers of all kinds. The fantastic adventure of our Chobin begins right by the sea one spring morning. While he was thinking of the strangest things as usual, he was disturbed by a noise, so he stood up and went to the source of this
noise, at that point he found a barrel that pushed by the waves of the sea continues to crash upon the rocks. He picked up the bottle and saw that it contained a message, opened it and found a parchment bearing the following sentence: 
Bring the right object before the king's throne of the Turks and you will be rewarded with a stupendous treasure. 

 Chobin did not have it repeated twice and immediately began his fantastic journey with his boat. You will control our Chobin in his adventure,
but be careful to direct him to the right island with the right object, otherwise poor Chobin will suffer a bad end! 
 
Published in several Italian game compilations, including Special Program N°43 (05/1988) supplement: RUN/STOP The 64 Magic Games N°1, Hit Parade 64 N°65 (03/1992) and Hit Parade C64 n.31 (Febbraio 1989).

Despite the game's name, there was no Chobin I.

214961.overview: Clef Climber is a game where the player is given a tone that corresponds to a certain musical note and must match the note being played. Lower difficulties provide a constant tone to refer to and visual help on the note being used. Higher difficulties provide a single playing of the tone and no visual help.

214963.overview: Originally created for publication in Italy, this action game by Luigi Recanatese  has you in charge of a ladybird\ladybug as she moves around the garden and was intended for release in 1986. In 2004 the game was updated and debugged (as much as you can a game about a ladybug) and Taper and Quorthon's fixes were made into an English version of the game, which was released as public domain.

214964.overview: A spruced up Mastermind clone with nice ambient music released by ACW Software in 1987. This version has 8 possible colors and multiple levels to challenge you.

214965.overview: A single player only Tetris style game created by Jörg Weese and published by Markt & Technik in 1993.

214966.overview: A game created by Paul Koller and released in 2018 in the 2018 C64 4KB Game Coding Competition, Good Old 8-Bit Games #1 and in Reset Magazine. It is a 4k game where you whip around a bullet trail to destroy the baddies, try to survive and rack up as much points as possible. You aren't shooting the bullets, they follow behind you like the tail of a kite. Watch out for the plusses, they may be invulnerable.

214967.overview:
Cross Chase by Fabrizio Caruso is an action game for the Commodore 64 built with the CROSS-LIB framework.

The game's goal is to lure the "ghosts" into the mines and possibly kill the "skull" by repeatedly using the gun. You have to avoid all enemies, the mines, all walls, rockets and chasing missiles. All flashing items have positive effects and can grant you some special powers. Discover the 10 items. If you use the gun against the skull and/or the missiles and rockets, you can unlock some special secret items. There are 20 different levels including 4 boss levels.

214983.overview: One of the first things that will catch your attention of this game is the evolution of your weapon. At first, you can only fire one arrow at once then when you start killing horde members (especially the white ones) they will give you speed, fast in shooting, triple shooting arrows, arrows to increase your stuff weapon and points. Beware of the red foes because they will constantly shoot at you. It is important that you have good aim, as you have limited arrows.

214984.overview: A shooter where you need to shoot all the enemies. The game was created by Fabrizio Caruso and released in April of 2021. Some enemies mrequite several shots to take out. You can also pick up treasures and additional bullets. Created with Cross-Lib a retro-hardware abstraction layer for coding "universal" games with the very same code for hundreds of mostly 8-bit systems (consoles, computers, scientific calculators, hand-held consoles, arcade boards, hacked toy computers, etc.).

214985.overview: A Worm\Snake style game by Fabrizio Caruso, released in 2020 as part of the Cross-Lib toolkit, a retro-hardware abstraction layer for coding "universal" games with the very same code for hundreds of mostly 8-bit systems (consoles, computers, scientific calculators, hand-held consoles, arcade boards, hacked toy computers, and so forth).

214986.overview: As the name suggests, the game is about crosses and circles. We fly around the board and catch all the circles that appear. They come from the right side of the board. The difficulty for us here are the aforementioned crosses, placed flat at different distances from each other, in addition, the board is not too large, so a bit tight there. If we take the cross twice by mistake, then we lose life and fall down. Created by Jan Zimmermann and published in 64'er 1993/09.

214987.overview:
Another time, East of Andromeda...
The planet of Ariiance was a happy place, or so it seemed. The two major countries, Keriiod and Febronce managed an uneasy peace, but underneath this facade lay a deep hate for each other. All went well until on e day when the Febronce and Keriiod leaders fell into a dispute. From that moment on, the countries were at war. The war raged for many years without a result until the two leaders reached an agreement. If one of them could conquer more than half the alliance, the rest of the land would be forfeited to them. And so it was...

215194.overview:
Cloud Strike is a 1-player arcade game for the Commodore 64.

The player controls a small plane that moves in all directions, and can fire laterally left and right. The player can shoot incoming enemy vehicles, and tries to pick up falling pilots. The player must pick up 9 pilots to move to the next level with faster moving enemies. The player starts with 5 lives, and it's game over when all are lost.

215195.overview:
You are in the Pharaoh's tomb. You must collect al the gold coins and get out of the tomb as fast as you can. This won't be easy because the tomb is haunted by the ghost of the Pharaoh's architect. You can choose two different skill levels for additional challenge in this 1983 collect'em up game. The tomb is a maze with golden coins in all the passageways. You must move through the maze collecting the coins. A ghost appears, causing the
doors to change position. You cannot escape 'til you have all the coins.

215495.overview:
CBM Poker Tournament (also called Speech Poker Tournament) is a single player poker game for the Commodore 64. It uses The Software Automatic Mouth (SAM) for the in-game speech. Despite being released and published by Commodore themselves, the game is considered slightly politically incorrect, as many of the opponents in the game utter words such as "arse, f*ck, and shit" when they have to fold.

The amount of money you start off is not a set amount. It starts with giving you a random amount of money.

216131.overview:
A puzzle game created by Tim Hartnell & Brett Hale and published in 1984 in the book "The Big Fat Book of Commodore 64 Games".
